## Introduction

Linear covariance propagation is a method for analyzing the evolution of uncertainty in a state vector over time.
This blog post aims to demonstrate the importance of choosing the correct state representation for linear covariance propagation in environments involving relative spacecraft dynamics. 
Specifically, we will study two state representations: the first using Cartesian coordinates represented in the Radial, In-Track, Cross-Track (RIC) frame 
propagated with the Clohessy-Wiltshire (CW) linearized equations of motion, 
and the second taking an orbital parameterization approach using Relative Orbital Elements (ROEs).

We will validate these methods through a Monte Carlo simulation using a nonlinear two-body dynamics propagator. It is important to perform these kinds of studies to validate spacecraft safety
during a mission.
